newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Davomas to double production capacity.
newsitem.headline: Davomas to double production capacity.

text.p: Indonesia's PT Davomas Abadi plans to double production capacity of cocoa butter to 160,000 tonnes by the year 1999 or 2000, the company president said on Friday.
Davomas, Indonesia's largest producer of cocoa butter, said in a statement released in Singapore it planned to add further production lines.

"We are very optimistic about the outlook of the world cocoa butter market where Davomas Abadi is a significant player. To keep pace with this anticipated growth, Davomas Abadi is undertaking a major expansion programme to more than double its production capacity to 160,000 tonnes per annum by 1999 or the year 2000," company president Hendrawan Setiadi was quoted as saying.

The company is also mulling going into chocolate production because of the country's huge potential market since Indonesia has a population of 200 million people and a low consumption rate, Hendrawan said.
"Davomas Abadi is also looking into the possibility of diversifying downstream into the production of chocolate or confectionary products," he said.
The diversification will take the form of establishing links with established chocolate producers in Europe like Switzerland. The company hopes to start the programme in 1998, the statement said.
Davomas is controlled by the same group as PT Fiskaragung Perkasa, the biggest producer of iodised salt in Indonesia.
